transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, my wife actually pushed me to come in. I guess... what brings me in is that I just don't feel real happiness anymore. Or closeness, really. Even when she tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or, you know, when something at work goes well... I just feel empty. I can't seem to feel those good emotions at all anymore.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
It's been... well, this has really been going on since the retrofit accident. That was about a year and seven months ago now.
Do you ever experience unwanted, distressing memories of the accident popping into your mind?

Yeah, I do. It happens pretty often, actually. It doesn't take much to set it off... just normal things at work. A standard plant alarm, looking at a retrofit checklist, or even just the smell of hot metal. It just throws me right back to seeing him on the floor, and hearing everyone yelling for help.
Do you find yourself trying to avoid people, places, conversations, or situations that remind you of the accident?

Yeah, I definitely do. I avoid that specific production line whenever I can. If it needs checking, I... I just send someone else to walk it instead of going down there myself. And if people start talking about the rollout or the investigation, I just shut the conversation down right away. I really don't want any part of those discussions.
